hardConstraints.description: No Anthropic model may use API credits, Nous, or OpenRouter for this program.

Grok 4.5 dispatches only through the prepaid Nous Portal lane in-program (PRD §15, plan §2). This session's OpenRouter-routed review predates program alignment and is not a standing exception; a future in-program Grok call outside the prepaid transport requires a PRD amendment (plan §6 open question 6 -- Nous-hosted Grok availability is not yet confirmed).

Mechanical verification runs via deterministic scripts and tests, never model judgment (PRD §15). This is not one of the ten §2 task classes; it deliberately has zero RoutingCandidate entries anywhere in modelTable. The sentinel modelFamily 'other' is banned on every transport here as a machine-evaluable guarantee that no candidate may ever claim that family for this concern -- see the top-level notes for why this is the schema's closest expression of 'has no model candidates'.

budgetCeilings.notes: All ceilings are conservative operator-tunable placeholders -- plan §5 P1 states 'the router recommends, human confirms' and names no binding dollar figures. Revise once real telemetry (CWR-P1-2/P1-3, outside this tranche) establishes actual per-stage cost distributions.

notes: Runtime model id mapping: claude.ts's curated MODEL_OPTIONS picker still lists 4-5 generation ids (claude-opus-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-5) while apps/daemon/src/runtimes/usage-tracking.ts already prices the 5-generation ids used in this policy (claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-fable-5) -- the claude runtime forwards an arbitrary --model string, so this policy uses the usage-tracking convention (the actual billing-relevant id) rather than the stale picker list. The picker list needs a refresh; that is not this tranche's scope.

Runtime model id mapping: codex.ts's curated MODEL_OPTIONS picker still lists 5.5-era ids (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, ...) while usage-tracking.ts already prices gpt-5.6-sol/terra/luna, used in this policy for the same reason as the Claude note above.

Runtime model id mapping: apps/daemon/src/runtimes/defs/antigravity.ts has no clean slug for Gemini 3.1 Pro -- its curated model id IS its display label, 'Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)'. This policy uses that exact runtime id rather than inventing a slug like 'gemini-3.1-pro', per this task's instruction to follow the runtime's own id conventions.

Runtime model id mapping: apps/daemon/src/runtimes/defs/grok-build.ts's curated model list tops out at the grok-4.20 generation and has no dedicated Nous-lane runtime among the daemon's 26 runtime defs; this policy names grok-4.5 (the plan's verified anchor) and lane 'nous' as a forward declaration for when a Nous-routed dispatch path exists. Plan §6 open question 6 explicitly flags that Nous-hosted Grok availability is not yet confirmed at P0 -- this row does not resolve that question, it only encodes the intended target once it is.

The prd-15-mechanical-verification-deterministic-only hard constraint uses modelFamily 'other' banned on every transport as the closest machine-evaluable expression of 'this concern has zero model candidates' -- the RoutingPolicyHardConstraint shape has no dedicated 'excluded task class' field. As long as no real model in modelTable ever carries modelFamily 'other' (none does here), the constraint holds trivially and by construction.

laneChains encodes the generic subscription-oauth -> prepaid -> metered-api fallback tier order (plan §2 'Lane realism') per starting lane. It does not itself intersect with hardConstraints -- e.g. an anthropic candidate's lane chain still lists 'nous' downstream even though the anthropic hard constraint forbids that transport. Applying hardConstraints (including allowedTransports) before ever consulting a lane chain is the P2 admission-control layer's job (out of this tranche's scope), not this policy document's.

Effort fields are 'inherit' everywhere §2 names a model without a parenthetical effort -- the only §2 cell that states one is Opus 5 '(high)' for art-direction-ia-brief-analysis's primary. Do not read 'inherit' as 'low priority'; it means 'the plan is silent, so this policy does not invent a value.'

Kimi K3 has no published per-token price in plan §2 -- only '1M ctx' is stated. No price row is carried for it (do not invent one); estimated-cost budgeting for Kimi-routed candidates has no policy-level anchor until a price is sourced. DeepSeek V4-Flash's $0.14/$0.28 anchor IS sourced and is at cache-miss (plan §2); one-shot ingestion work earns few cache hits (Grok F5), so cache-miss is the conservative budgeting anchor used here.

otherModelPriceRows entries omit effectiveDate: plan §2 states these as current verified anchors with no onset date, and only the two sonnetPriceRows entries carry a plan-sourced date (the 2026-08-31 boundary, plus the pre-boundary row it replaces).
